demos.code:
"""Candidate-carrier screening report.

Reproduces the registered verdict of the experiment and then applies the
aperiodicity screen to a list of candidate positional carriers, printing for
each one the period (if any), the composition drift its period permits, the
guaranteed surviving excess, and the accept/reject decision.

This is the practical pay-off of the theory: any carrier that factors through
the integers mod m can be excluded on paper, before a single expensive sieve
run, whenever m / L falls below the drift budget (rho - 1) / (rho + 1).
"""

from __future__ import annotations

from typing import Callable, Dict, List, Optional, Sequence, Tuple

RHO_MEASURED: float = 1.1774          # raw mid-window excess ratio
DRIFT_MEASURED: float = 0.00269       # measured composition drift (0.269 %)
SE_REGISTERED: float = 0.0432
SE_CALIBRATED: float = 0.0411
WINDOW_LENGTH: int = 100_000
N_DEFAULT: int = 8051                 # 83 * 97


def required_drift(rho: float) -> float:
    return (rho - 1.0) / (rho + 1.0)


def surviving_excess(rho: float, delta: float) -> float:
    return rho * (1.0 - delta) / (1.0 + delta) - 1.0


def registered_verdict() -> None:
    print("=" * 74)
    print("REGISTERED VERDICT (raw amplitude rule)")
    print("=" * 74)
    amp = RHO_MEASURED - 1.0
    surv = surviving_excess(RHO_MEASURED, DRIFT_MEASURED)
    print(f"  raw amplitude                 {amp:.4f} +- {SE_REGISTERED:.4f}"
          f"   (z = {amp / SE_REGISTERED:.2f})")
    print(f"  measured composition drift    {DRIFT_MEASURED:.5f}")
    print(f"  guaranteed surviving excess   {surv:.4f}")
    print(f"  registered bar 2*SE           {2 * SE_REGISTERED:.4f}"
          f"   cleared: {surv > 2 * SE_REGISTERED}")
    print(f"  null-calibrated 2*SE          {2 * SE_CALIBRATED:.4f}"
          f"   cleared: {surv > 2 * SE_CALIBRATED}")
    print(f"  drift budget (rho-1)/(rho+1)  {required_drift(RHO_MEASURED):.4f}"
          f"   ({required_drift(RHO_MEASURED) / DRIFT_MEASURED:.0f}x the measured drift)")
    print("  verdict: H0 -- the excess SURVIVES the divisibility mixture.")
    print()


def legendre_symbol(v: int, p: int) -> int:
    r = v % p
    if r == 0:
        return 0
    return 1 if pow(r, (p - 1) // 2, p) == 1 else -1


def candidate_carriers(n: int) -> List[Tuple[str, Callable[[int], object], Optional[int]]]:
    """(name, classifier, period or None if aperiodic)."""
    return [
        ("divisibility grid (2,3,5,7)",
         lambda j: ((j * j - n) % 2 == 0, (j * j - n) % 3 == 0,
                    (j * j - n) % 5 == 0, (j * j - n) % 7 == 0), 210),
        ("parity of j",
         lambda j: j % 2, 2),
        ("divisibility grid up to 19",
         lambda j: tuple((j * j - n) % p == 0 for p in (2, 3, 5, 7, 11, 13, 17, 19)),
         2 * 3 * 5 * 7 * 11 * 13 * 17 * 19),
        ("Legendre symbol of v mod 11",
         lambda j: legendre_symbol(j * j - n, 11), 11),
        ("Legendre symbol of v mod 1009",
         lambda j: legendre_symbol(j * j - n, 1009), 1009),
        ("low 8 bits of v",
         lambda j: (j * j - n) % 256, 256),
        ("v is a quadratic residue mod 10007",
         lambda j: legendre_symbol(j * j - n, 10007), 10007),
        ("size class: which decile of the scan j lies in",
         lambda j: min(9, (10 * j) // WINDOW_LENGTH), None),
        ("boundary class: v above the truncation threshold",
         lambda j: 1 if j * j - n > (WINDOW_LENGTH // 2) ** 2 else 0, None),
    ]


def screen() -> None:
    print("=" * 74)
    print("APERIODICITY SCREEN  (window length L = {:,})".format(WINDOW_LENGTH))
    print("=" * 74)
    d_star = required_drift(RHO_MEASURED)
    print(f"  drift budget delta* = {d_star:.4f}\n")
    header = f"  {'carrier':<50}{'period':>14}{'m/L':>10}{'verdict':>16}"
    print(header)
    print("  " + "-" * (len(header) - 2))
    for name, _f, period in candidate_carriers(N_DEFAULT):
        if period is None:
            print(f"  {name:<50}{'aperiodic':>14}{'--':>10}{'SURVIVES':>16}")
            continue
        bound = period / WINDOW_LENGTH
        per_txt = f"{period:,}" if period < 10 ** 8 else f"{period:.2e}"
        if period >= WINDOW_LENGTH:
            verdict = "needs a census"
        else:
            verdict = "rejected" if bound < d_star else "needs a census"
        print(f"  {name:<50}{per_txt:>14}{bound:>10.5f}{verdict:>16}")
    print()
    print("  'needs a census': the O(1) bound alone does not exclude it, so its")
    print("  composition drift must be measured directly (Algorithm 1).")
    print("  Every periodic carrier whose period is a small fraction of the window")
    print("  is rejected with no data pass: its mixture family is a ray, so it")
    print("  removes 0% of the excess.  Only aperiodic carriers -- size, boundary,")
    print("  valuation effects -- remain as candidate positional mechanisms.")
    print()


def surviving_excess_table() -> None:
    print("=" * 74)
    print("HOW MUCH EXCESS SURVIVES, AS A FUNCTION OF PERMITTED DRIFT")
    print("=" * 74)
    print(f"  {'delta':>10}{'shrink factor':>18}{'surviving excess':>20}{'above 2SE?':>14}")
    print("  " + "-" * 60)
    for delta in (0.0, 0.00269, 0.005, 0.01, 0.02, 0.04, 0.0815, 0.12):
        factor = (1 - delta) / (1 + delta)
        surv = RHO_MEASURED * factor - 1
        print(f"  {delta:>10.5f}{factor:>18.6f}{surv:>20.6f}"
              f"{str(surv > 2 * SE_REGISTERED):>14}")
    print()


def main() -> None:
    print()
    registered_verdict()
    screen()
    surviving_excess_table()


if __name__ == "__main__":
    main()

algorithms.name: Window Composition Census and Maximum Relative Drift
algorithms.description: Measures how much the class composition of a scan window changes as the window slides along the index line. For a classifier f of the sieve index j, a window length L and a set of start positions, it tabulates the population of every class at every start and returns the maximum relative drift delta_max, the quantity that must be compared against the drift budget (rho - 1)/(rho + 1) to decide whether the classifier could possibly explain a positional excess. The naive cost is O(|starts| * L) classifier evaluations; for a classifier known to be m-periodic one full period suffices, reducing the cost to O(m + |starts|), and the theory then predicts delta_max = 0 exactly whenever m divides L. Applied to the divisibility grid of v = j^2 - N with L = 210 it returns delta_max = 0 for every N, which is the structural content of the measured flatness.
algorithms.pseudocode:
INPUT:  classifier f : Z -> C, window length L, start positions A
OUTPUT: table of class populations, maximum relative drift delta_max

1  for each a in A:
2      counts[a] <- empty map from class to integer
3      for i = 0 to L - 1:
4          c <- f(a + i)
5          counts[a][c] <- counts[a][c] + 1
6  classes <- union of the keys of all counts[a]
7  delta_max <- 0
8  for each c in classes:
9      lo <- min over a of counts[a][c]
10     hi <- max over a of counts[a][c]
11     delta_max <- max(delta_max, (hi - lo) / max(1, lo))
12 return (counts, delta_max)

REMARK: if f is m-periodic and m divides L, steps 1-11 provably return
        delta_max = 0, and only one start needs to be evaluated.
algorithms.code:
"""Algorithm 1 — Window composition census.

Measures, for a candidate classifier f of the sieve index j, how much the class
composition of a window of length L drifts as the window slides along the line.
The output delta_max is the quantity that the drift budget (rho-1)/(rho+1) must
be compared against.
"""

from __future__ import annotations

from typing import Callable, Dict, Hashable, List, Sequence, Tuple

Class = Hashable


def class_counts(f: Callable[[int], Class], start: int, length: int) -> Dict[Class, int]:
    """Population of every class in the window {start, ..., start + length - 1}.

    Cost: O(length) classifier evaluations.
    """
    counts: Dict[Class, int] = {}
    for i in range(length):
        c = f(start + i)
        counts[c] = counts.get(c, 0) + 1
    return counts


def composition_census(
    f: Callable[[int], Class],
    starts: Sequence[int],
    length: int,
) -> Tuple[List[Dict[Class, int]], float]:
    """Tabulate the composition at every start and return the maximum relative drift.

    Returns (tables, delta_max) where

        delta_max = max_c  (max_a count(a, c) - min_a count(a, c))
                           / max(1, min_a count(a, c)).

    A value of exactly 0 certifies flat composition on the sampled starts, which
    by the collapse theorem forces 0% removal of any positional excess.

    Cost: O(|starts| * length).
    """
    tables = [class_counts(f, a, length) for a in starts]
    classes: set = set()
    for t in tables:
        classes |= set(t)
    delta_max = 0.0
    for c in classes:
        vals = [t.get(c, 0) for t in tables]
        lo, hi = min(vals), max(vals)
        delta_max = max(delta_max, (hi - lo) / max(1, lo))
    return tables, delta_max


def divisibility_cell(n: int) -> Callable[[int], Tuple[bool, bool, bool, bool]]:
    """The 16-cell divisibility classifier of v = j^2 - N over the primes 2,3,5,7."""
    def f(j: int) -> Tuple[bool, bool, bool, bool]:
        v = j * j - n
        return (v % 2 == 0, v % 3 == 0, v % 5 == 0, v % 7 == 0)
    return f


if __name__ == "__main__":
    n = 8051
    tables, drift = composition_census(
        divisibility_cell(n), starts=[0, 1, 97, -4321, 10**7], length=210
    )
    print("cell populations of the first window:")
    for c in sorted(tables[0], key=lambda t: tuple(map(int, t))):
        print("   ", tuple(int(b) for b in c), tables[0][c])
    print("maximum relative composition drift over all window starts:", drift)

algorithms.name: Flank-Fitted Mixture Baseline and Measurement of the Removal Fraction
algorithms.description: Implements the corrective model whose failure the theory explains. Given a measured profile T, a reference shape B and per-class reference curves S_c on a grid of window positions, it fits per-class rates kappa_c by ridge-regularised least squares on the flank bins only — the score region around the peak is withheld so the feature cannot influence its own explanation — forms the corrected baseline PRED = sum_c kappa_c S_c, and reports the relative mid-window excess over PRED alongside the excess over B, together with the removal fraction. The ridge term implements shrinkage toward the global flank rate and makes the problem well-posed even when the design matrix is rank-deficient, which is exactly the situation under flat composition. Cost is O(n|C|^2) to build the Gram matrix plus O(|C|^3) to solve it. Under flat composition the returned removal fraction is zero to floating-point precision, whatever solver is used, because the fitted prediction is necessarily a scalar multiple of B.
algorithms.pseudocode:
INPUT:  grid t[0..n-1], measurement T, references S_c for c in C,
        score window [lo, hi], ridge parameter lambda
OUTPUT: rates kappa, excess over B, excess over PRED, removal fraction

1  flank <- { i : t[i] < lo or t[i] > hi }
2  total[i] <- sum over c of S_c(t[i])
3  kappa_bar <- (sum_{i in flank} T[i] * total[i])
                / (sum_{i in flank} total[i]^2)          // global flank rate
4  G[c][c'] <- sum_{i in flank} S_c(t[i]) * S_c'(t[i]) + lambda * [c = c']
5  r[c]     <- sum_{i in flank} T[i] * S_c(t[i]) + lambda * kappa_bar
6  kappa    <- solve G kappa = r                          // symmetric, PD
7  PRED[i]  <- sum over c of kappa[c] * S_c(t[i])
8  R_B[i]   <- T[i] / B[i];      R_M[i] <- T[i] / PRED[i]
9  E_B <- R_B[peak]/R_B[flank] - 1
10 E_M <- R_M[peak]/R_M[flank] - 1
11 return (kappa, E_B, E_M, 1 - E_M / E_B)

THEOREM: if S_c = w_c * B for all c, then PRED = K * B with
         K = sum_c kappa[c] * w_c, hence E_M = E_B and the removal is 0.
algorithms.code:
"""Algorithm 2 — Flank-fitted mixture baseline and removal fraction.

Fits per-class rates kappa_c to a measured hit profile T on the flanks of the
scan window only (the score region is withheld), forms the corrected baseline
PRED = sum_c kappa_c S_c, and reports how much of the mid-window relative excess
the correction removed.

When the class references have flat composition, S_c(t) = w_c B(t), the design
matrix has rank 1, PRED is a scalar multiple of B, and the reported removal is
exactly 0 up to floating-point noise -- the collapse theorem in executable form.
"""

from __future__ import annotations

from typing import Dict, Hashable, List, Sequence, Tuple

Class = Hashable


def _solve_ridge(a: List[List[float]], b: List[float]) -> List[float]:
    """Solve a symmetric positive-definite system by Gaussian elimination."""
    n = len(b)
    m = [row[:] + [b[i]] for i, row in enumerate(a)]
    for col in range(n):
        piv = max(range(col, n), key=lambda r: abs(m[r][col]))
        m[col], m[piv] = m[piv], m[col]
        p = m[col][col]
        if abs(p) < 1e-15:
            continue
        for r in range(n):
            if r == col:
                continue
            factor = m[r][col] / p
            for k in range(col, n + 1):
                m[r][k] -= factor * m[col][k]
    out = []
    for i in range(n):
        out.append(m[i][n] / m[i][i] if abs(m[i][i]) > 1e-15 else 0.0)
    return out


def fit_mixture(
    grid: Sequence[float],
    target: Sequence[float],
    refs: Dict[Class, Sequence[float]],
    score_window: Tuple[float, float] = (0.45, 0.85),
    lam: float = 5.0,
) -> Dict[Class, float]:
    """Ridge-regularised least squares for the per-class rates, fitted on flanks.

    Minimises  sum_{t in flank} (T(t) - sum_c kappa_c S_c(t))^2
               + lam * sum_c (kappa_c - kappa_bar)^2,
    with kappa_bar the global flank rate.  The ridge term makes the rank-1
    design well-posed and implements shrinkage toward the global rate.

    Cost: O(n |C|^2 + |C|^3).
    """
    classes = list(refs)
    lo, hi = score_window
    flank = [i for i, t in enumerate(grid) if not (lo <= t <= hi)]
    total = [sum(refs[c][i] for c in classes) for i in range(len(grid))]
    num = sum(target[i] * total[i] for i in flank)
    den = sum(total[i] * total[i] for i in flank)
    kbar = num / den if den else 0.0

    k = len(classes)
    gram = [[sum(refs[ci][i] * refs[cj][i] for i in flank) + (lam if a == b else 0.0)
             for b, cj in enumerate(classes)] for a, ci in enumerate(classes)]
    rhs = [sum(target[i] * refs[c][i] for i in flank) + lam * kbar for c in classes]
    sol = _solve_ridge(gram, rhs)
    return {classes[a]: sol[a] for a in range(k)}


def mixture_prediction(
    rates: Dict[Class, float], refs: Dict[Class, Sequence[float]], n_pts: int
) -> List[float]:
    return [sum(rates[c] * refs[c][i] for c in refs) for i in range(n_pts)]


def relative_excess(residual: Sequence[float], i_peak: int, i_flank: int) -> float:
    return residual[i_peak] / residual[i_flank] - 1.0


def removal_fraction(
    grid: Sequence[float],
    target: Sequence[float],
    shape: Sequence[float],
    refs: Dict[Class, Sequence[float]],
    i_peak: int,
    i_flank: int,
) -> Tuple[float, float, float]:
    """Return (excess over shape, excess over mixture, removal fraction).

    The removal fraction is 1 - excess_mixture / excess_shape; the collapse
    theorem predicts 0 whenever the references have flat composition.
    """
    rates = fit_mixture(grid, target, refs)
    pred = mixture_prediction(rates, refs, len(grid))
    r_shape = [target[i] / shape[i] for i in range(len(grid))]
    r_mix = [target[i] / pred[i] for i in range(len(grid))]
    e_shape = relative_excess(r_shape, i_peak, i_flank)
    e_mix = relative_excess(r_mix, i_peak, i_flank)
    removal = 1.0 - e_mix / e_shape if e_shape else float("nan")
    return e_shape, e_mix, removal

algorithms.name: Aperiodicity Screen: Rejecting Candidate Carriers by the Scale-Free Drift Budget
algorithms.description: The practical pay-off of the theory. To absorb a relative excess rho - 1 a mixture must have composition drift at least delta* = (rho - 1)/(rho + 1); for an m-periodic classifier the drift over a window of length L is at most m/L. The screen therefore rejects any candidate carrier with m/L < delta* in constant time, without touching the data, and falls back on a measured composition census when the period is unknown or comparable to the window. Also included is a period detector that searches for the smallest modulus at which a black-box classifier repeats, cost O(max_period * probes). For the measured excess 0.1774 the budget is 8.15%, so at a scan window of 100000 indices every residue carrier of modulus below about 8000 is excluded on paper — including the sixteen-cell divisibility grid, parity, all small-prime Legendre symbols and all low-bit patterns.
algorithms.pseudocode:
INPUT:  raw excess ratio rho, candidate classifier f, window length L
OUTPUT: accept / reject, with a certificate

1  delta_star <- (rho - 1) / (rho + 1)          // scale-free drift budget
2  m <- known period of f, or detect_period(f), or NONE
3  if m is not NONE and m / L < delta_star:
4      return REJECT with certificate
5             "surviving excess >= rho (1 - m/L)/(1 + m/L) - 1 > 0"
6  // period unknown or too large: measure the drift directly
7  (counts, delta_max) <- composition_census(f, starts, L)
8  if delta_max < delta_star:
9      return REJECT with certificate
10            "surviving excess >= rho (1 - delta_max)/(1 + delta_max) - 1 > 0"
11 return ACCEPT: f is a genuine positional candidate, run the full fit

COMPLEXITY: O(1) in the periodic branch, O(|starts| * L) otherwise.

visualizations.name: The Mixture Family Collapses onto a Ray
visualizations.description: Two panels drawn from the same synthetic experiment. On the left, the Dickman reference shape B(t), the measured profile T(t) with its bump at t = 0.65, and a fan of sixteen-cell mixture predictions generated from random non-negative rate vectors: every one of them is a rescaled copy of the single curve B, never a curve with a bump of its own. On the right, the residuals T/PRED for the same random rate vectors, each normalised at the flank: they lie exactly on top of the residual over B, with the peak pinned at t = 0.65 and the amplitude pinned at 0.1774. This is the collapse theorem and the exact 0% removal, drawn.
visualizations.code:
"""Visualization 1 — The mixture family collapses onto a ray.

Left panel: the Dickman reference shape B(t), the measured profile T(t) with its
mid-window bump at t = 0.65, and a fan of sixteen-cell mixture predictions drawn
from random non-negative rate vectors.  Every one of them is a scalar multiple
of B: the fan is a family of rescaled copies of a single curve, never a curve
with a bump.

Right panel: the residuals T/PRED for the same rate vectors, each normalised at
the flank.  They coincide exactly -- the bump is untouched, whatever the rates.
This is the collapse theorem, drawn.

Requires: numpy, matplotlib.
"""

from __future__ import annotations

import math
import random
from typing import Dict, List, Tuple

import matplotlib.pyplot as plt
import numpy as np

Cell = Tuple[bool, bool, bool, bool]


def cell(n: int, j: int) -> Cell:
    v = j * j - n
    return (v % 2 == 0, v % 3 == 0, v % 5 == 0, v % 7 == 0)


def window_populations(n: int, start: int = 0, length: int = 210) -> Dict[Cell, int]:
    counts: Dict[Cell, int] = {}
    for i in range(length):
        c = cell(n, start + i)
        counts[c] = counts.get(c, 0) + 1
    return counts


def dickman_rho(u: float, steps: int = 3000) -> float:
    if u <= 1.0:
        return 1.0 if u > 0 else 0.0
    grid_max = max(2.0, math.ceil(u) + 1.0)
    h = grid_max / steps
    vals = [1.0 if i * h <= 1.0 else 0.0 for i in range(steps + 1)]

    def interp(x: float) -> float:
        if x <= 0.0:
            return 0.0
        if x <= 1.0:
            return 1.0
        k = x / h
        i = int(k)
        if i >= steps:
            return vals[steps]
        return vals[i] * (1 - (k - i)) + vals[i + 1] * (k - i)

    for i in range(1, steps + 1):
        x = i * h
        if x <= 1.0:
            continue
        vals[i] = max(0.0, vals[i - 1] - (h / x) * interp(x - 1.0))
    return interp(u)


def main() -> None:
    n = 8051
    t = np.linspace(0.0, 1.0, 401)
    shape = np.array([dickman_rho(2.0 + 0.8 * x) for x in t])
    bump = 1.0 + 0.1774 * np.exp(-0.5 * ((t - 0.65) / 0.10) ** 2)
    target = shape * bump

    pops = window_populations(n)
    cells: List[Cell] = list(pops)

    rng = random.Random(20260831)
    fig, axes = plt.subplots(1, 2, figsize=(13, 5))

    ax = axes[0]
    ax.plot(t, shape, color="#1f3b70", lw=2.5, label=r"reference shape $B(t)$")
    ax.plot(t, target, color="#c0392b", lw=2.5,
            label=r"measurement $T(t)$ (bump at $t=0.65$)")
    for k in range(12):
        rates = {c: rng.uniform(0.2, 2.0) for c in cells}
        pred = sum(rates[c] * pops[c] for c in cells) / sum(pops.values()) * shape
        ax.plot(t, pred, color="#7f8c8d", lw=0.9, alpha=0.65,
                label="16-cell mixtures (random rates)" if k == 0 else None)
    ax.set_xlabel("window coordinate $t$")
    ax.set_ylabel("hit density")
    ax.set_title("Every mixture is a rescaled copy of one shape")
    ax.legend(fontsize=9)
    ax.grid(alpha=0.25)

    ax = axes[1]
    i_flank = int(0.05 * (len(t) - 1))
    base_resid = target / shape
    ax.plot(t, base_resid / base_resid[i_flank], color="#1f3b70", lw=2.5,
            label="residual over $B$")
    for k in range(12):
        rates = {c: rng.uniform(0.2, 2.0) for c in cells}
        K = sum(rates[c] * pops[c] for c in cells) / sum(pops.values())
        resid = target / (K * shape)
        ax.plot(t, resid / resid[i_flank], color="#e67e22", lw=0.9, alpha=0.7,
                label="residual over mixtures" if k == 0 else None)
    ax.axvline(0.65, color="#2c3e50", ls="--", lw=1)
    ax.axhline(1.1774, color="#27ae60", ls=":", lw=1.5,
               label=r"amplitude $0.1774$")
    ax.set_xlabel("window coordinate $t$")
    ax.set_ylabel("residual, normalised at the flank")
    ax.set_title("Removal is exactly 0%: the curves coincide")
    ax.legend(fontsize=9)
    ax.grid(alpha=0.25)

    fig.suptitle("Divisibility is a rate dial, not a position dial", fontsize=14)
    fig.tight_layout()
    fig.savefig("ray_collapse.png", dpi=160)
    print("wrote ray_collapse.png")


if __name__ == "__main__":
    main()

"""Visualization 2 — Flat composition versus a genuine position dial.

Top panel: the population of each of the sixteen divisibility cells of
v = j^2 - N, plotted as the window of 210 consecutive j slides along the line.
Every trace is exactly horizontal -- window composition is independent of
position, which is why sixteen free rates buy no positional freedom at all.

Middle panel: the same census for an aperiodic "size" carrier that bins j by how
far it has travelled across the scan; its composition drifts strongly with
position, so it is a position dial in the exact sense of the theory.

Bottom panel: the drift budget.  Absorbing a relative excess rho - 1 requires
composition drift at least (rho - 1)/(rho + 1); the measured excess 0.1774 needs
8.1%, while the divisibility grid supplies 0.269%.

Requires: numpy, matplotlib.
"""

from __future__ import annotations

from typing import Dict, List, Tuple

import matplotlib.pyplot as plt
import numpy as np

Cell = Tuple[bool, bool, bool, bool]


def cell(n: int, j: int) -> Cell:
    v = j * j - n
    return (v % 2 == 0, v % 3 == 0, v % 5 == 0, v % 7 == 0)


def census(n: int, start: int, length: int = 210) -> Dict[Cell, int]:
    counts: Dict[Cell, int] = {}
    for i in range(length):
        c = cell(n, start + i)
        counts[c] = counts.get(c, 0) + 1
    return counts


def size_carrier(j: int, origin: int, span: int, bins: int = 4) -> int:
    """An aperiodic carrier: which quarter of the total scan the index sits in."""
    frac = (j - origin) / span
    return max(0, min(bins - 1, int(frac * bins)))


def main() -> None:
    n = 8051
    starts = list(range(0, 2000, 10))

    labels: List[Cell] = sorted(census(n, 0), key=lambda c: tuple(map(int, c)))
    series = {c: [census(n, a).get(c, 0) for a in starts] for c in labels}

    span = 4000
    bin_series = {b: [] for b in range(4)}
    for a in starts:
        counts = {b: 0 for b in range(4)}
        for i in range(210):
            counts[size_carrier(a + i, 0, span)] += 1
        for b in range(4):
            bin_series[b].append(counts[b])

    fig, axes = plt.subplots(3, 1, figsize=(11, 12))

    ax = axes[0]
    for c in labels:
        ax.plot(starts, series[c], lw=2,
                label="(" + "".join("1" if b else "0" for b in c) + ")")
    ax.set_ylim(-5, 60)
    ax.set_xlabel("window start $a$")
    ax.set_ylabel("cell population in a 210-window")
    ax.set_title("Divisibility grid: composition is exactly flat in position "
                 "(a RATE dial)")
    ax.legend(ncol=4, fontsize=8, title="cell $(2|v,3|v,5|v,7|v)$")
    ax.grid(alpha=0.25)

    ax = axes[1]
    for b in range(4):
        ax.plot(starts, bin_series[b], lw=2, label=f"size bin {b}")
    ax.set_xlabel("window start $a$")
    ax.set_ylabel("class population in a 210-window")
    ax.set_title("An aperiodic size carrier: composition drifts with position "
                 "(a POSITION dial)")
    ax.legend(fontsize=9)
    ax.grid(alpha=0.25)

    ax = axes[2]
    rho = np.linspace(1.0, 1.6, 300)
    ax.plot(rho - 1, (rho - 1) / (rho + 1), color="#1f3b70", lw=2.5,
            label=r"required drift $(\rho-1)/(\rho+1)$")
    ax.axvline(0.1774, color="#c0392b", ls="--", lw=1.5,
               label="measured excess 0.1774")
    ax.axhline(0.00269, color="#27ae60", ls=":", lw=2,
               label="measured drift 0.269%")
    ax.plot([0.1774], [(1.1774 - 1) / (1.1774 + 1)], "o", color="#c0392b", ms=8)
    ax.annotate("needs 8.1%", xy=(0.1774, 0.0815), xytext=(0.24, 0.10),
                arrowprops=dict(arrowstyle="->", color="#2c3e50"))
    ax.set_xlabel(r"relative excess $\rho - 1$")
    ax.set_ylabel("composition drift required to absorb it")
    ax.set_title("Drift budget: a scale-free necessary condition for absorption")
    ax.legend(fontsize=9)
    ax.grid(alpha=0.25)

    fig.tight_layout()
    fig.savefig("composition_census.png", dpi=160)
    print("wrote composition_census.png")


if __name__ == "__main__":
    main()

interactive_layout:
# Divisibility Is a Rate Dial, Not a Position Dial ### A guided tour: why sixteen free parameters could not move a bump by one part in ten thousand --- ## 0 · The five-minute version A sieve walks along the values $v = j^2 - N$ and keeps the ones that are **smooth** — those that factor completely over a small prime base. Plotting how often it succeeds against the position $t \in [0,1]$ inside the scan window, and dividing by the classical prediction, reveals a stubborn bump: at $t = 0.65$ the hit rate sits about $17.7\%$ above where it should be. The obvious explanation is bookkeeping. Values divisible by $3$, or by $5$, are *already* part of the way to being smooth, so the candidate population is a mixture of sub-populations with different rates. If that mixture drifted across the window, the bump would be an illusion. So the natural corrective model was fitted: sixteen cells, one per divisibility pattern of $v$ over $\{2,3,5,7\}$, each with its own free rate. It removed **exactly zero percent** of the bump. This page explains why the answer had to be zero — and what that tells us about where the real mechanism must live. --- ## 1 · The tape that repeats Start with the object at the heart of everything: the *cell* of a candidate, $$c(v) \;=\; \bigl(2 \mid v,\; 3\mid v,\; 5 \mid v,\; 7 \mid v\bigr),$$ one of sixteen possibilities. Colour each $j$ by the cell of $v = j^2 - N$ and you get a coloured tape. Play with it: switch primes on and off, change $N$, and slide the tape against a copy of itself until they lock. {{interactive_demo:1}}
Why the tape must repeat — the one-line proof The cell of $v$ depends only on $v$ modulo $2, 3, 5$ and $7$, hence only on $v$ modulo $210 = 2\cdot3\cdot5\cdot7$. And $$(j + 210)^2 - N \;=\; (j^2 - N) \;+\; 210\,(2j + 210),$$ so $v(j+210) \equiv v(j) \pmod{210}$ and the cell label satisfies $c(j+210) = c(j)$ for **every** integer $N$ and every $j$. Nothing about $N$ — its size, its factorization, its residues — enters the argument. More generally, for any modulus $m$, $$(j+m)^2 - N \;\equiv\; j^2 - N \pmod m,$$ so *any* classification of $v$ by its residue mod $m$ is $m$-periodic in $j$. Remember this: it is the reason an entire family of candidate explanations dies at once in §5.
The instant consequence is the statement that runs the whole story. > **Flat Composition Theorem.** For every $N$, every cell $c$ and every starting point $a$, the number of $j \in \{a, a+1, \dots, a+209\}$ whose value lies in cell $c$ is the same. The composition of a window does not depend on where the window is.
Proof: a sliding-window telescope Let $h(i) = 1$ if $j = a+i$ lands in cell $c$, else $0$. Summing $h$ over $\{0,1,\dots,210\}$ in two ways, $$\sum_{i=0}^{209} h(i+1) \;+\; h(0) \;=\; \sum_{i=0}^{209} h(i) \;+\; h(210).$$ By periodicity $h(210) = h(0)$, so the two remaining sums are equal. The left one counts the window starting at $a+1$, the right one the window starting at $a$. Shifting by one changes nothing; by induction, shifting by anything changes nothing. $\blacksquare$
Concretely, for $N = 8051 = 83 \times 97$, *every* window of $210$ consecutive candidates contains exactly $45 + 18 + 30 + 12$ values in the four cells with $j$ even, the same four counts again for $j$ odd, and precisely **zero** in every cell requiring $3 \mid v$ — because $8051 \equiv 2 \pmod 3$ is a quadratic non-residue, so $j^2 \equiv 8051$ has no solution modulo $3$ at all. --- ## 2 · Sixteen dials wired to one knob Here is where the algebra bites. Flat composition means each cell's reference curve is a fixed *fraction* of one common shape $B$: $$S_c(t) \;=\; w_c\,B(t).$$ Feed that into the mixture and watch the parameters evaporate: $$\mathrm{PRED}(t) \;=\; \sum_c \kappa_c S_c(t) \;=\; \Bigl(\sum_c \kappa_c w_c\Bigr) B(t) \;=\; K\cdot B(t).$$ Sixteen numbers in, one number out. In fact the set of *all* achievable predictions is exactly the ray $\{K \cdot B : K \in \mathbb{R}\}$: the model can change the volume, and nothing else. {{visualization:0}} Now go and turn the dials yourself. Randomise the rates as often as you like; slide the window; switch to a Legendre-symbol carrier, or to a bit-pattern carrier. Then switch to one of the two **aperiodic** carriers and watch what changes. {{interactive_demo:0}}
The three corollaries that make the null result exact Write $R(t) = T(t)/P(t)$ for the residual of the measurement $T$ against a baseline $P$, and let the *relative excess* be $R(t_0)/R(t_1) - 1$ between the peak $t_0$ and a flank $t_1$. 1. **Residual rescaling.** $T/\mathrm{PRED} = (T/B)/K$ — the mixture residual is the plain residual divided by a constant. 2. **Amplitude invariance.** A constant cancels from a ratio, so the relative excess over the mixture *equals* the relative excess over $B$. The removal fraction is identically $0$. 3. **Argmax invariance.** Dividing by a positive constant preserves every inequality $R(t) \le R(t_0)$, so the peak stays exactly where it was, at $t = 0.65$. And a fourth, for completeness: if the measurement is not proportional to $B$ at even two positions, then no mixture reproduces it at all.
> **The slogan.** *Divisibility is a rate dial, not a position dial.* It is worth being precise about what is **not** being claimed. The cell rates are real and strongly modulated: whether a prime $p$ divides any $v$ at all is governed by whether $N$ is a quadratic residue mod $p$, giving $0$, $1$ or $2$ roots and hence a rate of $0$, $1/p$ or $2/p$. In the measurement, fitted rates ranged over a factor of $2.2$. Divisibility matters enormously for *how many* smooth values there are. It says nothing about *where*. {{visualization:1}} --- ## 3 · Being honest: the drift budget Real compositions are flat only to measurement precision — here $0.269\%$. A negative result that leans on an idealization is worth little, so relax the hypothesis. If every cell's reference is within a relative factor $\delta$ of the exactly-flat value, the mixture is squeezed between $(1-\delta)KB$ and $(1+\delta)KB$, and the excess ratio $\rho$ can shrink by at most the factor $(1-\delta)/(1+\delta)$. Turning that around gives the single most portable statement in the whole development: > **Drift Budget.** To absorb a relative excess $\rho - 1$, the mixture's composition drift must satisfy > $$\delta \;\ge\; \frac{\rho - 1}{\rho + 1}.$$ For the measured $\rho - 1 = 0.1774$ that demands $\delta \ge 8.1\%$, against a measured $0.269\%$ — a factor of more than thirty. Note what the inequality does not mention: no bit length, no window length, no prime bound. It is scale-free, so the same test applies verbatim at any problem size. {{algorithm:2}}
Where the bound comes from Suppose the fitted baseline satisfies $P(t_0) \le (1+\delta)KB(t_0)$ at the peak and $P(t_1) \ge (1-\delta)KB(t_1)$ at the flank, and that the raw excess is $\rho$, i.e. $T(t_0)B(t_1) = \rho\,T(t_1)B(t_0)$. Then $$\frac{T(t_0)/P(t_0)}{T(t_1)/P(t_1)} \;=\;\frac{T(t_0)P(t_1)}{T(t_1)P(t_0)} \;\ge\;\frac{T(t_0)\,(1-\delta)KB(t_1)}{T(t_1)\,(1+\delta)KB(t_0)} \;=\;\rho\,\frac{1-\delta}{1+\delta}.$$ Setting the left side $\le 1$ (complete absorption) gives $\rho(1-\delta) \le 1+\delta$, i.e. $\delta \ge (\rho-1)/(\rho+1)$. With $\delta = 0.00269$ and $\rho = 1.1774$ the surviving excess is at least $0.1710$, comfortably above the registered detection bar $2\times0.0432 = 0.0864$ and above the more conservative null-calibrated $2 \times 0.0411 = 0.0822$.
--- ## 4 · The census, in code Everything above is checkable in a few lines. The first algorithm measures the composition drift of any candidate classifier; the second performs the flank-fitted mixture and reports the removal fraction that theory says must be zero. {{algorithm:0}} {{algorithm:1}} Run the whole pipeline end to end and watch the predicted numbers appear: a spread of $10^{-16}$ in $\mathrm{PRED}/B$, a removal fraction of $2\times10^{-16}$, a peak that stays at $t = 0.65$ to the last digit. {{demo:0}} --- ## 5 · One theorem, an entire family of suspects Divisibility by $2,3,5,7$ was only the first candidate. The natural follow-ups — larger primes, higher power residues, low bits of $j$, Legendre symbols $\left(\frac{j^2-N}{p}\right)$ at $p > 7$ — look like genuinely different hypotheses. They are not, because the argument used exactly one property: **periodicity**. > **Every classifier of $j$ that factors through $\mathbb{Z}/m\mathbb{Z}$ is $m$-periodic**, hence has flat composition on windows of length a multiple of $m$, hence spans a ray, hence removes exactly $0\%$. Even incommensurate windows are pinned down: two windows of length $L$ can differ in any class population by at most $L \bmod m < m$, a relative drift below $m/L$. Combine with the drift budget and you get a hard threshold — a residue carrier can absorb the excess only if its period is at least $8.1\%$ of the whole scan. {{demo:1}} The follow-up question has therefore sharpened into a genuine constraint: > **The carrier must be aperiodic.** Whatever concentrates smooth values near $t = 0.65$ cannot factor through $\mathbb{Z}/m\mathbb{Z}$ for any modulus $m$ dividing the window length. It is not a divisibility pattern, not a Legendre symbol, not a residue class, not a bit pattern of $j^2 - N$.
Isn't the framework just incapable of removing anything? No — and this is worth checking, because a vacuous negative result would be worthless. Allow a reference family whose cells drift with position. The simplest has two cells: one carrying the flat shape $B$, one carrying the measured profile $T$ itself. Fit it, and the mixture reproduces the measurement exactly, the residual becomes constant, and the excess is removed **completely**: $100\%$. And aperiodic carriers with position-dependent composition genuinely exist. The crude classifier "is $j \ge 0$?" puts an entire window in one class at $a = 0$ and the entire window in the other class just to the left of the origin — maximal composition drift, hence periodic at no modulus at all. Side by side: over a flat grid the fitting procedure preserves the excess exactly, for every choice of rates; over a positional family the very same procedure annihilates it. The $0\%$ is a fact about the arithmetic grid, not about the method.
--- ## 6 · Where to look next The surviving candidates are the classifiers that see **magnitude rather than residue**: the actual size of $v = j^2 - N$ as $j$ traverses the window (it grows monotonically, hence aperiodically), proximity to a truncation or logarithm-threshold boundary in the sieve, and $p$-adic valuations beyond mere divisibility — $v_p(v) \ge 2$ events are rarer and interact with the size gradient. Each of these can be pre-screened on paper before any expensive run, using the budget of §3. There is also a clean theoretical target. "Position dial" now has an exact meaning — non-invariance of window composition under translation — and for finite-valued classifiers that is essentially equivalent to periodicity. A classification theorem would say: a finite-valued classifier whose window composition drifts by more than $C/L$ is not almost periodic, and its Fourier–Bohr spectrum must contain an irrational frequency. That would replace the modulus-by-modulus screen with a single spectral criterion. Further reading on the ingredients: the [Dickman function](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dickman_function) that supplies the baseline shape, [smooth numbers](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Smooth_number) as the raw material of the sieve, the [quadratic sieve](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Quadratic_sieve) that scans $j^2 - N$, the [Legendre symbol](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Legendre_symbol) that decides which primes are alive, and [almost periodic functions](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Almost_periodic_function), the natural home of the classification theorem above. --- ## 7 · The transferable lesson When a feature in data refuses to die, the reflex is to add parameters. But parameters are worth only what their *span* is worth. Sixteen rate parameters over a periodic grid span a one-dimensional space — a single volume knob, useless against a feature that lives in position. Before adding a knob, ask what it can move. Sometimes the most informative thing a model can tell you is that it was never able to say anything at all.

import Mathlib

/-!
# The divisibility grid of `j² - N` is a rate dial, not a position dial (Part I)

Context: experiment 588c / paper 242.  A mid-window excess in the small-prime
sieve hit profile was tested against a **16-cell divisibility mixture baseline**:
each sieve value `v = j² - N` is labelled by its divisibility pattern
`(2 ∣ v, 3 ∣ v, 5 ∣ v, 7 ∣ v)`, giving `16` cells, and the baseline prediction is
`PRED(t) = Σ_c κ_c · S_c(t)` with per-cell rates `κ_c` fitted on the flanks.

The measurement found the class *composition* flat in the window coordinate
(max cell drift `0.269 %`), so the mixture had no positional freedom.  This file
proves the structural reason: **the cell label of `j² - N` is a periodic
function of `j` with period `210 = 2·3·5·7`, hence every window of `210`
consecutive `j` contains exactly the same number of members of every cell.**
Composition is therefore *exactly* position-independent, whatever `N` is.

Main results.

* `cellOf_periodic`, `cell_periodic` — the cell label is `210`-periodic.
* `windowCount_succ`, `windowCount_const` — the per-cell population of a window
  of `210` consecutive `j` does not depend on where the window starts.
* `two_dvd_iff_odd` — for odd `N`, bit `0` of the grid (`2 ∣ j² - N`) is exactly
  the parity of `j`: parity is *inside* the grid, not an extra carrier.
* `windowCount_8051_table`, `windowCount_8051_three_empty`,
  `windowCount_8051_parity_split`, `windowCount_8051_table_everywhere` — a
  kernel-checked rate table for `N = 8051 = 83·97`, and the same table at every
  window position.
* `sqCount_three`, `sqCount_five`, `sqCount_seven` — the per-prime rates are
  genuinely modulated (`0`, `1` or `2` roots mod `p`, i.e. rate `0`, `1/p` or
  `2/p`), so the "rate dial" really does turn; `windowCount_const` says it never
  turns *with position*.
-/

set_option maxRecDepth 8000

namespace RateDial

open Finset

/-! ## The 16 divisibility cells -/

/-- The divisibility pattern of `v` with respect to the primes `2, 3, 5, 7`:
one of `16` cells. -/
def cellOf (v : ℤ) : Bool × Bool × Bool × Bool :=
  (decide (2 ∣ v), decide (3 ∣ v), decide (5 ∣ v), decide (7 ∣ v))

/-- The cell of the sieve value `v = j² - N`. -/
def cell (N j : ℤ) : Bool × Bool × Bool × Bool := cellOf (j ^ 2 - N)

/-- The cell label only sees `v` modulo `210 = 2 · 3 · 5 · 7`. -/
theorem cellOf_periodic (v k : ℤ) : cellOf (v + 210 * k) = cellOf v := by
  have h2 : ((2:ℤ) ∣ v + 210 * k) ↔ (2:ℤ) ∣ v := by
    constructor <;> intro h <;> omega
  have h3 : ((3:ℤ) ∣ v + 210 * k) ↔ (3:ℤ) ∣ v := by
    constructor <;> intro h <;> omega
  have h5 : ((5:ℤ) ∣ v + 210 * k) ↔ (5:ℤ) ∣ v := by
    constructor <;> intro h <;> omega
  have h7 : ((7:ℤ) ∣ v + 210 * k) ↔ (7:ℤ) ∣ v := by
    constructor <;> intro h <;> omega
  simp only [cellOf, h2, h3, h5, h7]

/-- The cell of `j² - N` is a `210`-periodic function of `j`. -/
theorem cell_periodic (N j : ℤ) : cell N (j + 210) = cell N j := by
  have hv : (j + 210) ^ 2 - N = (j ^ 2 - N) + 210 * (2 * j + 210) := by ring
  simp only [cell, hv, cellOf_periodic]

/-! ## Window populations are position independent -/

/-- The number of `j` in the window `{a, a+1, …, a+209}` of `210` consecutive
integers whose sieve value lies in cell `c`. -/
def windowCount (N a : ℤ) (c : Bool × Bool × Bool × Bool) : ℕ :=
  ∑ i ∈ Finset.range 210, if cell N (a + i) = c then 1 else 0

/-- Shifting the window by one does not change any cell population. -/
theorem windowCount_succ (N a : ℤ) (c : Bool × Bool × Bool × Bool) :
    windowCount N (a + 1) c = windowCount N a c := by
  classical
  set h : ℕ → ℕ := fun i => if cell N (a + i) = c then 1 else 0 with hh
  have e1 : ∑ i ∈ range 211, h i = (∑ i ∈ range 210, h (i + 1)) + h 0 :=
    Finset.sum_range_succ' h 210
  have e2 : ∑ i ∈ range 211, h i = (∑ i ∈ range 210, h i) + h 210 :=
    Finset.sum_range_succ h 210
  have e3 : h 210 = h 0 := by
    have hcell : cell N (a + ((210 : ℕ) : ℤ)) = cell N (a + ((0 : ℕ) : ℤ)) := by
      have : a + ((210 : ℕ) : ℤ) = (a + ((0 : ℕ) : ℤ)) + 210 := by push_cast; ring
      rw [this, cell_periodic]
    simp only [hh, hcell]
  have e4 : windowCount N (a + 1) c = ∑ i ∈ range 210, h (i + 1) := by
    refine Finset.sum_congr rfl fun i _ => ?_
    have harg : a + 1 + ((i : ℕ) : ℤ) = a + (((i + 1 : ℕ)) : ℤ) := by push_cast; ring
    simp only [hh, harg]
  have e5 : windowCount N a c = ∑ i ∈ range 210, h i := rfl
  omega

/-- **Flat composition.**  Every window of `210` consecutive `j` has exactly the
same cell population: the divisibility grid carries no positional information. -/
theorem windowCount_const (N a : ℤ) (c : Bool × Bool × Bool × Bool) :
    windowCount N a c = windowCount N 0 c := by
  refine Int.induction_on a rfl (fun n ih => ?_) (fun n ih => ?_)
  · rw [windowCount_succ]; exact ih
  · have hstep := windowCount_succ N (-(n : ℤ) - 1) c
    have hEq : (-(n : ℤ) - 1) + 1 = -(n : ℤ) := by ring
    rw [hEq] at hstep
    rw [← hstep]
    exact ih

/-- Two windows anywhere on the line have identical composition. -/
theorem windowCount_eq (N a b : ℤ) (c : Bool × Bool × Bool × Bool) :
    windowCount N a c = windowCount N b c := by
  rw [windowCount_const N a c, windowCount_const N b c]

/-! ## Bit 0 of the grid is exactly `j`-parity -/

/-- For odd `N`, `2 ∣ j² - N` holds precisely when `j` is odd: the parity
"carrier" is a coordinate of the divisibility grid, not something outside it. -/
theorem two_dvd_iff_odd {N : ℤ} (hN : Odd N) (j : ℤ) :
    (2 : ℤ) ∣ j ^ 2 - N ↔ Odd j := by
  obtain ⟨m, hm⟩ := hN
  constructor
  · intro h
    rcases Int.even_or_odd j with he | ho
    · obtain ⟨k, hk⟩ := he
      exfalso
      rw [hk, hm] at h
      have hexp : (k + k) ^ 2 - (2 * m + 1) = 2 * (2 * k ^ 2 - m) - 1 := by ring
      rw [hexp] at h
      omega
    · exact ho
  · rintro ⟨k, hk⟩
    subst hk hm
    have : (2 * k + 1) ^ 2 - (2 * m + 1) = 2 * (2 * k ^ 2 + 2 * k - m) := by ring
    rw [this]
    exact ⟨_, rfl⟩

/-! ## The rates themselves are real: quadratic-residue modulation -/

/-- Mod `3` the number of `j` with `j² = N` is `1`, `2` or `0`: the `3 ∣ v` rate
is `1/3`, `2/3` or `0` times the generic `1/3`. -/
theorem sqCount_three (N : ZMod 3) :
    (Finset.univ.filter fun j : ZMod 3 => j ^ 2 = N).card =
      if N = 0 then 1 else if N = 1 then 2 else 0 := by revert N; decide

/-- Mod `5`: the same trichotomy, with two square classes. -/
theorem sqCount_five (N : ZMod 5) :
    (Finset.univ.filter fun j : ZMod 5 => j ^ 2 = N).card ≤ 2 ∧
      ((Finset.univ.filter fun j : ZMod 5 => j ^ 2 = N).card = 0 ∨
       (Finset.univ.filter fun j : ZMod 5 => j ^ 2 = N).card = 1 ∨
       (Finset.univ.filter fun j : ZMod 5 => j ^ 2 = N).card = 2) := by revert N; decide

/-- Mod `7`: idem; and the rate really is modulated, e.g. `N = 3` is a
non-residue (`0` roots) while `N = 1` has `2` roots. -/
theorem sqCount_seven :
    (Finset.univ.filter fun j : ZMod 7 => j ^ 2 = 3).card = 0 ∧
    (Finset.univ.filter fun j : ZMod 7 => j ^ 2 = 1).card = 2 := by decide

/-! ## A kernel-checked rate table

Real data for `N = 8051 = 83 · 97` (odd, `8051 ≡ 2 mod 3`, a quadratic
non-residue mod `3`).  These are the exact cell populations of a `210`-window;
by `windowCount_const` the very same numbers occur at *every* window position,
which is the content of the flat-composition finding. -/

section RateTable

set_option maxRecDepth 1000000

/-- The eight nonempty cells of `N = 8051`, exactly. -/
theorem windowCount_8051_table :
    windowCount 8051 0 (false, false, false, false) = 45 ∧
    windowCount 8051 0 (false, false, false, true) = 18 ∧
    windowCount 8051 0 (false, false, true, false) = 30 ∧
    windowCount 8051 0 (false, false, true, true) = 12 ∧
    windowCount 8051 0 (true, false, false, false) = 45 ∧
    windowCount 8051 0 (true, false, false, true) = 18 ∧
    windowCount 8051 0 (true, false, true, false) = 30 ∧
    windowCount 8051 0 (true, false, true, true) = 12 :=
  ⟨rfl, rfl, rfl, rfl, rfl, rfl, rfl, rfl⟩

/-- All cells with `3 ∣ v` are empty, because `8051` is a quadratic non-residue
mod `3`: a per-cell rate of exactly `0`.  The dial is genuinely turned. -/
theorem windowCount_8051_three_empty (b₀ b₂ b₃ : Bool) :
    windowCount 8051 0 (b₀, true, b₂, b₃) = 0 := by
  revert b₀ b₂ b₃
  decide

/-- The parity bit splits the window exactly in half: `105` odd `j` and `105`
even `j`, matching `two_dvd_iff_odd`. -/
theorem windowCount_8051_parity_split :
    windowCount 8051 0 (true, false, false, false) +
      windowCount 8051 0 (true, false, false, true) +
      windowCount 8051 0 (true, false, true, false) +
      windowCount 8051 0 (true, false, true, true) = 105 := by
  decide

/-- The table is positional data-free: the same populations occur in the window
starting at any `a`, e.g. at `a = 1234` and `a = -77777`. -/
theorem windowCount_8051_table_everywhere (a : ℤ) :
    windowCount 8051 a (false, false, false, false) = 45 ∧
    windowCount 8051 a (false, false, true, true) = 12 ∧
    windowCount 8051 a (false, true, false, false) = 0 := by
  refine ⟨?_, ?_, ?_⟩
  · rw [windowCount_const 8051 a]; exact windowCount_8051_table.1
  · rw [windowCount_const 8051 a]; exact windowCount_8051_table.2.2.2.1
  · rw [windowCount_const 8051 a]; exact windowCount_8051_three_empty false false false

end RateTable

end RateDial

import Mathlib
import Shared.MixtureRateDialCells

/-!
# A flat-composition mixture baseline is a ray: it cannot absorb a positional excess (Part II)

Context: experiment 588c / paper 242.  A mid-window excess of the sieve hit
profile survived a `16`-cell divisibility mixture baseline
`PRED(t) = Σ_c κ_c · S_c(t)` with amplitude `0.1774 ± 0.0432` (`z = 4.11`) and
`0 %` removal relative to the single-`α` baseline.  Part I
(`Shared.MixtureRateDialCells`) proved the *structural* reason the mixture had no
positional freedom: the divisibility cell of `j² - N` is `210`-periodic in `j`,
so the class composition of a window is exactly the same wherever the window is.

This file proves the *algebraic* consequence — the theorem behind the slogan
**"divisibility is a rate dial, not a position dial"**.

* `mixPred_eq_smul` — flat composition collapses the whole `|C|`-parameter
  mixture family to a single scalar multiple of the common shape `B`.
* `mixture_family_eq_ray` — the set of achievable predictions is *exactly* the
  ray `{K · B}`; the mixture has one degree of freedom (a rate) and none in `t`.
* `mixPred_no_positional_freedom` — any two mixtures are proportional, pointwise
  in `t`.
* `relExcess_invariant`, `removal_eq_zero` — the residual's relative mid-window
  excess is *identical* to the one over the single-shape baseline: the removal
  fraction is exactly `0 %`, matching the measurement.
* `peak_position_invariant`, `argmax_invariant` — the peak stays at the same `t`.
* `mixture_cannot_fit_nonproportional` — if the measurement is not proportional
  to `B`, no mixture reproduces it.
* `mixPred_drift_bounds`, `excess_ratio_lower_bound_div` — the robust version:
  if composition is flat only up to a relative drift `δ`, the mixture can shrink
  the excess by at most the factor `(1-δ)/(1+δ)`.
* `absorption_requires_drift`, `drift_budget_measured` — the inverse, scale-free
  reading: absorbing a relative excess `ρ - 1` needs composition drift at least
  `(ρ-1)/(ρ+1)`, i.e. `8.1 %` for the measured excess against a measured drift of
  `0.269 %`.
* `H0_excess_survives_measured`, `H0_excess_beats_bar` — the registered verdict
  with the measured numbers: with the measured drift `δ = 0.269 %` and raw
  excess `0.1774`, the mixture residual excess is still `≥ 0.1710`, far above the
  registered bar `2 · SE = 0.0864` (and above the null-calibrated scale as well).
* `divisibility_mixture_excess_survives` — the capstone, with the mixture built
  from the *actual* `210`-periodic cell populations of Part I.
-/

namespace RateDial

open Finset

variable {C : Type*} [Fintype C]

/-! ## Flat composition and the mixture prediction -/

/-- A cell-resolved reference model has **flat composition** if every cell's
reference sum is a fixed fraction `w c` of one common positional shape `B`.
This is what Part I proves for the divisibility grid of `j² - N`. -/
def FlatComposition (S : C → ℝ → ℝ) (w : C → ℝ) (B : ℝ → ℝ) : Prop :=
  ∀ c t, S c t = w c * B t

/-- The mixture prediction `PRED(t) = Σ_c κ_c · S_c(t)`. -/
noncomputable def mixPred (κ : C → ℝ) (S : C → ℝ → ℝ) (t : ℝ) : ℝ := ∑ c, κ c * S c t

/-- The residual of a measured profile against a baseline. -/
noncomputable def resid (T P : ℝ → ℝ) (t : ℝ) : ℝ := T t / P t

/-- The relative excess of a residual between the peak `t₀` and a flank `t₁`
(the amplitude reported by the experiment). -/
noncomputable def relExcess (R : ℝ → ℝ) (t₀ t₁ : ℝ) : ℝ := R t₀ / R t₁ - 1

/-- **Collapse.**  Under flat composition every mixture is a scalar multiple of
the single common shape: the `|C|` rate parameters buy exactly one number. -/
theorem mixPred_eq_smul {S : C → ℝ → ℝ} {w : C → ℝ} {B : ℝ → ℝ}
    (hflat : FlatComposition S w B) (κ : C → ℝ) (t : ℝ) :
    mixPred κ S t = (∑ c, κ c * w c) * B t := by
  rw [mixPred, Finset.sum_mul]
  exact Finset.sum_congr rfl fun c _ => by rw [hflat c t]; ring

/-- **No positional freedom.**  Any two mixtures over a flat-composition grid are
proportional as functions of `t`. -/
theorem mixPred_no_positional_freedom {S : C → ℝ → ℝ} {w : C → ℝ} {B : ℝ → ℝ}
    (hflat : FlatComposition S w B) (κ κ' : C → ℝ) (s t : ℝ) :
    mixPred κ S t * mixPred κ' S s = mixPred κ S s * mixPred κ' S t := by
  rw [mixPred_eq_smul hflat, mixPred_eq_smul hflat, mixPred_eq_smul hflat,
    mixPred_eq_smul hflat]
  ring

/-- **The mixture family is a ray.**  If some cell has a nonzero share, the set
of achievable predictions is exactly `{K · B : K ∈ ℝ}` — one rate dial, no
positional dial. -/
theorem mixture_family_eq_ray [DecidableEq C] {S : C → ℝ → ℝ} {w : C → ℝ} {B : ℝ → ℝ}
    (hflat : FlatComposition S w B) {c₀ : C} (hc₀ : w c₀ ≠ 0) :
    {f : ℝ → ℝ | ∃ κ : C → ℝ, mixPred κ S = f} = {f : ℝ → ℝ | ∃ K : ℝ, f = fun t => K * B t} := by
  ext f
  constructor
  · rintro ⟨κ, rfl⟩
    exact ⟨∑ c, κ c * w c, funext fun t => mixPred_eq_smul hflat κ t⟩
  · rintro ⟨K, rfl⟩
    refine ⟨fun c => if c = c₀ then K / w c₀ else 0, funext fun t => ?_⟩
    rw [mixPred_eq_smul hflat]
    have hsum : (∑ c, (if c = c₀ then K / w c₀ else 0) * w c) = K := by
      rw [Finset.sum_eq_single c₀]
      · rw [if_pos rfl]
        field_simp
      · intro b _ hb; simp [hb]
      · intro h; exact absurd (Finset.mem_univ c₀) h
    rw [hsum]

/-! ## The residual is unchanged: removal is exactly zero -/

/-- The residual against a flat mixture is the residual against `B`, rescaled by
the single fitted rate `K`. -/
theorem resid_mix_eq {S : C → ℝ → ℝ} {w : C → ℝ} {B T : ℝ → ℝ}
    (hflat : FlatComposition S w B) (κ : C → ℝ) (t : ℝ) :
    resid T (mixPred κ S) t = resid T B t / (∑ c, κ c * w c) := by
  simp only [resid, mixPred_eq_smul hflat]
  rw [div_div, mul_comm (B t) (∑ c, κ c * w c)]

/-- **Invariance of the amplitude.**  The relative mid-window excess of the
residual over the mixture baseline equals the one over the single common shape:
the mixture removes none of it. -/
theorem relExcess_invariant {S : C → ℝ → ℝ} {w : C → ℝ} {B T : ℝ → ℝ}
    (hflat : FlatComposition S w B) (κ : C → ℝ) {t₀ t₁ : ℝ}
    (hK : (∑ c, κ c * w c) ≠ 0) (hT : T t₁ ≠ 0) (hB : B t₁ ≠ 0) :
    relExcess (resid T (mixPred κ S)) t₀ t₁ = relExcess (resid T B) t₀ t₁ := by
  have h1 : resid T B t₁ ≠ 0 := div_ne_zero hT hB
  simp only [relExcess, resid_mix_eq hflat]
  congr 1
  field_simp

/-- **Removal is exactly `0 %`** (the pre-named corroboration of the experiment). -/
theorem removal_eq_zero {S : C → ℝ → ℝ} {w : C → ℝ} {B T : ℝ → ℝ}
    (hflat : FlatComposition S w B) (κ : C → ℝ) {t₀ t₁ : ℝ}
    (hK : (∑ c, κ c * w c) ≠ 0) (hT : T t₁ ≠ 0) (hB : B t₁ ≠ 0) :
    relExcess (resid T (mixPred κ S)) t₀ t₁ - relExcess (resid T B) t₀ t₁ = 0 := by
  rw [relExcess_invariant hflat κ hK hT hB, sub_self]

/-- **The peak does not move.**  If `t₀` dominates the single-shape residual on a
set `W`, it dominates the mixture residual on `W` as well. -/
theorem peak_position_invariant {S : C → ℝ → ℝ} {w : C → ℝ} {B T : ℝ → ℝ}
    (hflat : FlatComposition S w B) (κ : C → ℝ) {W : Set ℝ} {t₀ : ℝ}
    (hK : 0 < ∑ c, κ c * w c)
    (hmax : ∀ t ∈ W, resid T B t ≤ resid T B t₀) :
    ∀ t ∈ W, resid T (mixPred κ S) t ≤ resid T (mixPred κ S) t₀ := by
  intro t ht
  rw [resid_mix_eq hflat, resid_mix_eq hflat]
  exact (div_le_div_iff_of_pos_right hK).mpr (hmax t ht)

/-- Strict version: a strict interior peak stays a strict interior peak. -/
theorem argmax_invariant {S : C → ℝ → ℝ} {w : C → ℝ} {B T : ℝ → ℝ}
    (hflat : FlatComposition S w B) (κ : C → ℝ) {t t₀ : ℝ}
    (hK : 0 < ∑ c, κ c * w c) (hlt : resid T B t < resid T B t₀) :
    resid T (mixPred κ S) t < resid T (mixPred κ S) t₀ := by
  rw [resid_mix_eq hflat, resid_mix_eq hflat]
  exact (div_lt_div_iff_of_pos_right hK).mpr hlt

/-- **Non-fittability.**  If the measurement is not proportional to the common
shape at two positions, then no mixture reproduces it. -/
theorem mixture_cannot_fit_nonproportional {S : C → ℝ → ℝ} {w : C → ℝ} {B T : ℝ → ℝ}
    (hflat : FlatComposition S w B) {t₀ t₁ : ℝ}
    (hnp : T t₀ * B t₁ ≠ T t₁ * B t₀) (κ : C → ℝ) :
    mixPred κ S ≠ T := by
  intro hEq
  apply hnp
  have h0 : T t₀ = (∑ c, κ c * w c) * B t₀ := by
    rw [← hEq]; exact mixPred_eq_smul hflat κ t₀
  have h1 : T t₁ = (∑ c, κ c * w c) * B t₁ := by
    rw [← hEq]; exact mixPred_eq_smul hflat κ t₁
  rw [h0, h1]; ring

/-! ## Robust version: composition flat only up to a relative drift `δ` -/

/-- With per-cell relative drift at most `δ`, the mixture is squeezed between
`(1-δ)` and `(1+δ)` times the exactly-flat prediction. -/
theorem mixPred_drift_bounds {S : C → ℝ → ℝ} {w : C → ℝ} {B : ℝ → ℝ} {κ : C → ℝ}
    {δ t : ℝ} (hκ : ∀ c, 0 ≤ κ c)
    (hdrift : ∀ c, |S c t - w c * B t| ≤ δ * (w c * B t)) :
    (1 - δ) * ((∑ c, κ c * w c) * B t) ≤ mixPred κ S t ∧
      mixPred κ S t ≤ (1 + δ) * ((∑ c, κ c * w c) * B t) := by
  have hlow : ∀ c, (1 - δ) * (w c * B t) ≤ S c t := by
    intro c
    have h := abs_le.mp (hdrift c)
    nlinarith [h.1]
  have hhigh : ∀ c, S c t ≤ (1 + δ) * (w c * B t) := by
    intro c
    have h := abs_le.mp (hdrift c)
    nlinarith [h.2]
  have hlowsum : (1 - δ) * ((∑ c, κ c * w c) * B t) = ∑ c, κ c * ((1 - δ) * (w c * B t)) := by
    rw [Finset.sum_mul, Finset.mul_sum]
    exact Finset.sum_congr rfl fun c _ => by ring
  have hhighsum : (1 + δ) * ((∑ c, κ c * w c) * B t) = ∑ c, κ c * ((1 + δ) * (w c * B t)) := by
    rw [Finset.sum_mul, Finset.mul_sum]
    exact Finset.sum_congr rfl fun c _ => by ring
  constructor
  · rw [hlowsum]
    exact Finset.sum_le_sum fun c _ => by
      exact mul_le_mul_of_nonneg_left (hlow c) (hκ c)
  · rw [hhighsum]
    exact Finset.sum_le_sum fun c _ => by
      exact mul_le_mul_of_nonneg_left (hhigh c) (hκ c)

/-- Multiplicative core of the robustness estimate: with `P₀ ≤ (1+δ)·K·B₀` and
`P₁ ≥ (1-δ)·K·B₁` and raw excess ratio `ρ = (T₀/B₀)/(T₁/B₁)`, the mixture
residual ratio is at least `ρ·(1-δ)/(1+δ)`. -/
theorem excess_ratio_lower_bound_mul {T0 T1 P0 P1 B0 B1 K δ ρ : ℝ}
    (hδ0 : 0 ≤ δ) (hδ1 : δ < 1) (hB0 : 0 < B0) (hB1 : 0 < B1)
    (hT0 : 0 ≤ T0) (hT1 : 0 < T1)
    (hP0le : P0 ≤ (1 + δ) * (K * B0)) (hP1ge : (1 - δ) * (K * B1) ≤ P1)
    (hρ : T0 * B1 = ρ * (T1 * B0)) :
    ρ * (1 - δ) * (T1 * P0) ≤ (1 + δ) * (T0 * P1) := by
  have hpos : 0 < T1 * B0 := mul_pos hT1 hB0
  have hρ0 : 0 ≤ ρ := by
    by_contra hc
    push_neg at hc
    nlinarith [mul_nonneg hT0 hB1.le]
  have h1δ : (0:ℝ) ≤ 1 - δ := by linarith
  have hA : 0 ≤ ρ * (1 - δ) * T1 := mul_nonneg (mul_nonneg hρ0 h1δ) hT1.le
  have step1 : ρ * (1 - δ) * (T1 * P0) ≤ ρ * (1 - δ) * (T1 * ((1 + δ) * (K * B0))) := by
    have h := mul_le_mul_of_nonneg_left hP0le hA
    linarith [h]
  have key : ρ * (1 - δ) * (T1 * ((1 + δ) * (K * B0))) = (1 + δ) * (T0 * ((1 - δ) * (K * B1))) := by
    have hsym : ρ * (T1 * B0) = T0 * B1 := hρ.symm
    calc ρ * (1 - δ) * (T1 * ((1 + δ) * (K * B0)))
        = (1 - δ) * (1 + δ) * K * (ρ * (T1 * B0)) := by ring
      _ = (1 - δ) * (1 + δ) * K * (T0 * B1) := by rw [hsym]
      _ = (1 + δ) * (T0 * ((1 - δ) * (K * B1))) := by ring
  have step3 : (1 + δ) * (T0 * ((1 - δ) * (K * B1))) ≤ (1 + δ) * (T0 * P1) :=
    mul_le_mul_of_nonneg_left (mul_le_mul_of_nonneg_left hP1ge hT0) (by linarith)
  linarith [step1, key, step3]

/-- Division form of the robustness estimate. -/
theorem excess_ratio_lower_bound_div {T0 T1 P0 P1 B0 B1 K δ ρ : ℝ}
    (hδ0 : 0 ≤ δ) (hδ1 : δ < 1) (hB0 : 0 < B0) (hB1 : 0 < B1)
    (hT0 : 0 ≤ T0) (hT1 : 0 < T1) (hP0 : 0 < P0) (hP1 : 0 < P1)
    (hP0le : P0 ≤ (1 + δ) * (K * B0)) (hP1ge : (1 - δ) * (K * B1) ≤ P1)
    (hρ : T0 * B1 = ρ * (T1 * B0)) :
    ρ * (1 - δ) / (1 + δ) ≤ (T0 / P0) / (T1 / P1) := by
  have hmul := excess_ratio_lower_bound_mul (K := K) hδ0 hδ1 hB0 hB1 hT0 hT1 hP0le hP1ge hρ
  have hδpos : 0 < 1 + δ := by linarith
  have hkey : (T0 / P0) / (T1 / P1) = (T0 * P1) / (T1 * P0) := by
    field_simp
  rw [hkey]
  refine (div_le_div_iff₀ hδpos (mul_pos hT1 hP0)).mpr ?_
  nlinarith

theorem H0_excess_survives_measured {T0 T1 P0 P1 B0 B1 K : ℝ}
    (hB0 : 0 < B0) (hB1 : 0 < B1) (hT0 : 0 ≤ T0) (hT1 : 0 < T1)
    (hP0 : 0 < P0) (hP1 : 0 < P1)
    (hP0le : P0 ≤ (1 + 269/100000) * (K * B0))

factor of almost two — and also clears twice the null-calibrated standard error

theorem H0_excess_beats_bar {T0 T1 P0 P1 B0 B1 K : ℝ}
    (hB0 : 0 < B0) (hB1 : 0 < B1) (hT0 : 0 ≤ T0) (hT1 : 0 < T1)
    (hP0 : 0 < P0) (hP1 : 0 < P1)
    (hP0le : P0 ≤ (1 + 269/100000) * (K * B0))

/-- **Drift budget (inverse form).**  A mixture can only absorb the excess
entirely if its composition drift is at least `(ρ - 1)/(ρ + 1)`, where `ρ` is the
raw excess ratio.  This is a scale-free necessary condition: it does not mention
the data geometry, so it transfers across bit lengths unchanged. -/
theorem absorption_requires_drift {T0 T1 P0 P1 B0 B1 K δ ρ : ℝ}
    (hδ0 : 0 ≤ δ) (hδ1 : δ < 1) (hB0 : 0 < B0) (hB1 : 0 < B1)
    (hT0 : 0 ≤ T0) (hT1 : 0 < T1) (hP0 : 0 < P0) (hP1 : 0 < P1)
    (hP0le : P0 ≤ (1 + δ) * (K * B0)) (hP1ge : (1 - δ) * (K * B1) ≤ P1)
    (hρ : T0 * B1 = ρ * (T1 * B0))
    (habs : (T0 / P0) / (T1 / P1) ≤ 1) :
    (ρ - 1) / (ρ + 1) ≤ δ := by
  have hbound := excess_ratio_lower_bound_div (K := K) hδ0 hδ1 hB0 hB1 hT0 hT1 hP0 hP1
    hP0le hP1ge hρ
  have hρ0 : 0 ≤ ρ := by
    by_contra hc
    push_neg at hc
    nlinarith [mul_nonneg hT0 hB1.le, mul_pos hT1 hB0]
  have hδpos : 0 < 1 + δ := by linarith
  have hle : ρ * (1 - δ) / (1 + δ) ≤ 1 := le_trans hbound habs
  have hmul : ρ * (1 - δ) ≤ 1 + δ := by
    rw [div_le_one hδpos] at hle
    linarith
  rw [div_le_iff₀ (by linarith : (0:ℝ) < ρ + 1)]
  nlinarith

/-- With the measured raw excess `ρ - 1 = 0.1774`, absorbing it needs a
composition drift of at least `8.1 %` — more than `30` times the measured
`0.269 %`. -/
theorem drift_budget_measured {T0 T1 P0 P1 B0 B1 K δ : ℝ}
    (hδ0 : 0 ≤ δ) (hδ1 : δ < 1) (hB0 : 0 < B0) (hB1 : 0 < B1)
    (hT0 : 0 ≤ T0) (hT1 : 0 < T1) (hP0 : 0 < P0) (hP1 : 0 < P1)
    (hP0le : P0 ≤ (1 + δ) * (K * B0)) (hP1ge : (1 - δ) * (K * B1) ≤ P1)
    (hρ : T0 * B1 = (11774/10000) * (T1 * B0))
    (habs : (T0 / P0) / (T1 / P1) ≤ 1) :
    (81 : ℝ)/1000 ≤ δ ∧ 30 * (269/100000 : ℝ) < δ := by
  have h := absorption_requires_drift (K := K) (ρ := 11774/10000) hδ0 hδ1 hB0 hB1 hT0 hT1
    hP0 hP1 hP0le hP1ge hρ habs
  norm_num at h
  constructor <;> linarith

/-- The cell-resolved reference sums of the experiment: the population of cell
`c` in the window at position `t`, weighted by the common (Dickman) shape `B`. -/
noncomputable def cellRefSum (N : ℤ) (B : ℝ → ℝ) (c : Bool × Bool × Bool × Bool) (t : ℝ) : ℝ :=
  (windowCount N ⌊t⌋ c : ℝ) * B t

/-- Part I says exactly this: the divisibility grid has flat composition. -/
theorem cellRefSum_flatComposition (N : ℤ) (B : ℝ → ℝ) :
    FlatComposition (cellRefSum N B) (fun c => (windowCount N 0 c : ℝ)) B := by
  intro c t
  simp only [cellRefSum, windowCount_const N ⌊t⌋ c]

/-- **Capstone (paper 242).**  For the real `16`-cell divisibility grid of
`v = j² - N`, no choice of per-cell rates `κ` removes any part of the
mid-window excess: the residual excess over the fitted mixture equals the
residual excess over the plain shape `B`, so removal is exactly `0 %`.
Divisibility is a rate dial, not a position dial. -/
theorem divisibility_mixture_excess_survives (N : ℤ) (B T : ℝ → ℝ)
    (κ : Bool × Bool × Bool × Bool → ℝ) {t₀ t₁ : ℝ}
    (hK : (∑ c, κ c * (windowCount N 0 c : ℝ)) ≠ 0) (hT : T t₁ ≠ 0) (hB : B t₁ ≠ 0) :
    relExcess (resid T (mixPred κ (cellRefSum N B))) t₀ t₁ = relExcess (resid T B) t₀ t₁ :=
  relExcess_invariant (cellRefSum_flatComposition N B) κ hK hT hB

/-- Contrapositive reading of the capstone: a nonzero mid-window excess over the
plain shape forces a nonzero excess over *every* divisibility mixture. -/
theorem divisibility_mixture_cannot_flatten (N : ℤ) (B T : ℝ → ℝ)
    (κ : Bool × Bool × Bool × Bool → ℝ) {t₀ t₁ : ℝ}
    (hK : (∑ c, κ c * (windowCount N 0 c : ℝ)) ≠ 0) (hT : T t₁ ≠ 0) (hB : B t₁ ≠ 0)
    (hexc : relExcess (resid T B) t₀ t₁ ≠ 0) :
    relExcess (resid T (mixPred κ (cellRefSum N B))) t₀ t₁ ≠ 0 := by
  rw [divisibility_mixture_excess_survives N B T κ hK hT hB]
  exact hexc

/-!
# No residue carrier is a position dial (Part III): the named follow-up, one family removed

Context: experiment 588c / paper 242 leaves the named follow-up *"identify the
non-divisibility carrier"*, with pre-named candidate family (i): `j`-arithmetic
beyond small-prime divisibility — higher-order residues of `v = j² - N`, bit
structure of `j`, quadratic-character / Legendre patterns mod `p > 7`.

This file removes **that entire family at once**, at every modulus and every
bit length.  The mechanism is the one isolated in Part I, but the divisibility
grid plays no special role in it:

> Every classifier of `j` that factors through `ZMod m` — divisibility patterns,
> Legendre symbols, higher power residues, low bit patterns, any Boolean
> combination of them — has *position independent* window composition as soon as
> the window length is a multiple of `m`.  By Part II its mixture family is a
> ray, so it removes exactly `0 %` of a positional excess.

Main results.

* `count_add`, `count_le` — basic window-count calculus.
* `count_const_of_period_dvd` — flat composition for any `m`-periodic classifier
  and window length a multiple of `m`.
* `count_drift_le_mod` — the *quantitative* version for a window length that is
  not a multiple: the composition of two windows can differ by at most
  `L % m < m` members, i.e. a relative drift `< m / L`.
* `periodicClass_of_zmod`, `residueCarrier_periodic`, `legendreCarrier_periodic`
  — every residue-type carrier of `v = j² - N` is periodic.
* `residue_mixture_excess_survives` — the capstone: the residual excess over any
  residue-class mixture equals the excess over the plain shape.
* `positional_carrier_is_aperiodic` — contrapositive and the actual content of
  the follow-up: **a carrier that moves the excess cannot factor through any
  `ZMod m` with `m ∣ L`; the non-divisibility carrier must be aperiodic in `j`.**
-/

namespace RateDial

open Finset

variable {α : Type*} [DecidableEq α]

/-! ## Periodic classifiers and window counts -/

/-- `f` classifies integers `m`-periodically. -/
def PeriodicClass (m : ℕ) (f : ℤ → α) : Prop := ∀ j : ℤ, f (j + m) = f j

/-- The number of `j` in the window `{a, …, a + L - 1}` with class `c`. -/
def count (f : ℤ → α) (a : ℤ) (L : ℕ) (c : α) : ℕ :=
  ∑ i ∈ Finset.range L, if f (a + i) = c then 1 else 0

theorem count_le (f : ℤ → α) (a : ℤ) (L : ℕ) (c : α) : count f a L c ≤ L := by
  calc count f a L c ≤ ∑ _i ∈ Finset.range L, 1 := by
        refine Finset.sum_le_sum fun i _ => ?_
        split <;> simp
    _ = L := by simp

/-- Windows concatenate. -/
theorem count_add (f : ℤ → α) (a : ℤ) (L₁ L₂ : ℕ) (c : α) :
    count f a (L₁ + L₂) c = count f a L₁ c + count f (a + L₁) L₂ c := by
  simp only [count]
  rw [Finset.sum_range_add]
  congr 1
  refine Finset.sum_congr rfl fun i _ => ?_
  have harg : a + ((L₁ + i : ℕ) : ℤ) = a + (L₁ : ℤ) + (i : ℤ) := by push_cast; ring
  rw [harg]

omit [DecidableEq α] in
/-- Periodicity iterates. -/
theorem periodic_add_natMul {m : ℕ} {f : ℤ → α} (hper : PeriodicClass m f) (j : ℤ) :
    ∀ k : ℕ, f (j + m * k) = f j := by
  intro k
  induction k with
  | zero => simp
  | succ n ih =>
      have harg : j + (m : ℤ) * ((n + 1 : ℕ) : ℤ) = (j + (m : ℤ) * (n : ℤ)) + (m : ℤ) := by
        push_cast; ring
      rw [harg, hper, ih]

/-- Shifting a window whose length is a multiple of the period preserves every
class population. -/
theorem count_succ_of_period {m : ℕ} {f : ℤ → α} (hper : PeriodicClass m f) (a : ℤ)
    {L q : ℕ} (hL : L = m * q) (c : α) :
    count f (a + 1) L c = count f a L c := by
  classical
  set h : ℕ → ℕ := fun i => if f (a + i) = c then 1 else 0 with hh
  have e1 : ∑ i ∈ range (L + 1), h i = (∑ i ∈ range L, h (i + 1)) + h 0 :=
    Finset.sum_range_succ' h L
  have e2 : ∑ i ∈ range (L + 1), h i = (∑ i ∈ range L, h i) + h L :=
    Finset.sum_range_succ h L
  have e3 : h L = h 0 := by
    have hfa : f (a + (L : ℤ)) = f (a + ((0 : ℕ) : ℤ)) := by
      have harg : a + (L : ℤ) = a + (m : ℤ) * (q : ℤ) := by rw [hL]; push_cast; ring
      rw [harg, periodic_add_natMul hper a q]
      norm_num
    simp only [hh, hfa]
  have e4 : count f (a + 1) L c = ∑ i ∈ range L, h (i + 1) := by
    refine Finset.sum_congr rfl fun i _ => ?_
    have harg : a + 1 + ((i : ℕ) : ℤ) = a + (((i + 1 : ℕ)) : ℤ) := by push_cast; ring
    simp only [hh, harg]
  have e5 : count f a L c = ∑ i ∈ range L, h i := rfl
  omega

/-- **Flat composition, general form.**  For an `m`-periodic classifier and a
window length that is a multiple of `m`, every window anywhere on the line has
exactly the same class populations. -/
theorem count_const_of_period_dvd {m : ℕ} {f : ℤ → α} (hper : PeriodicClass m f)
    {L q : ℕ} (hL : L = m * q) (a : ℤ) (c : α) :
    count f a L c = count f 0 L c := by
  refine Int.induction_on a rfl (fun n ih => ?_) (fun n ih => ?_)
  · rw [count_succ_of_period hper _ hL]; exact ih
  · have hstep := count_succ_of_period hper (-(n : ℤ) - 1) hL c
    have hEq : (-(n : ℤ) - 1) + 1 = -(n : ℤ) := by ring
    rw [hEq] at hstep
    rw [← hstep]
    exact ih

/-! ## Quantitative version: window length not a multiple of the period -/

/-- A window of `q` full periods contains exactly `q` copies of each class. -/
theorem count_fullPeriods {m : ℕ} {f : ℤ → α} (hper : PeriodicClass m f) (a : ℤ) (q : ℕ) (c : α) :
    count f a (m * q) c = q * count f 0 m c := by
  induction q generalizing a with
  | zero => simp [count]
  | succ n ih =>
      have hlen : m * (n + 1) = m * n + m := by ring
      rw [hlen, count_add, ih a]
      have hfull : count f (a + ((m * n : ℕ) : ℤ)) m c = count f 0 m c :=
        count_const_of_period_dvd hper (q := 1) (by ring) _ c
      rw [hfull]
      ring

/-- A window of length `m * q + r` splits into `q` full periods plus a remainder. -/
theorem count_split {m : ℕ} {f : ℤ → α} (hper : PeriodicClass m f) (a : ℤ) (q r : ℕ) (c : α) :
    count f a (m * q + r) c = q * count f 0 m c + count f (a + ((m * q : ℕ) : ℤ)) r c := by
  rw [count_add, count_fullPeriods hper a q]

/-- **Bounded drift.**  For an `m`-periodic classifier and an arbitrary window
length `L`, the population of a class in two windows differs by at most
`L % m < m`: a relative composition drift below `m / L`. -/
theorem count_drift_le_mod {m : ℕ} {f : ℤ → α} (hper : PeriodicClass m f)
    (a b : ℤ) (L : ℕ) (c : α) :
    count f a L c ≤ count f b L c + L % m := by
  have hL : L = m * (L / m) + L % m := (Nat.div_add_mod L m).symm
  have ha := count_split hper a (L / m) (L % m) c
  have hb := count_split hper b (L / m) (L % m) c
  rw [← hL] at ha hb
  have hbound := count_le f (a + ((m * (L / m) : ℕ) : ℤ)) (L % m) c
  omega

/-! ## Every residue-type carrier of `j` (and of `j² - N`) is periodic -/

omit [DecidableEq α] in
/-- Any classifier that factors through `ZMod m` is `m`-periodic. -/
theorem periodicClass_of_zmod (m : ℕ) (g : ZMod m → α) :
    PeriodicClass m (fun j : ℤ => g ((j : ZMod m))) := by
  intro j
  have : (((j + (m : ℤ)) : ℤ) : ZMod m) = ((j : ℤ) : ZMod m) := by
    push_cast
    simp
  simp only [this]

omit [DecidableEq α] in
/-- Higher-order residue carriers of the sieve value `v = j² - N`: any function of
`v mod m` — power residues, bit patterns, Legendre symbols — is `m`-periodic in
`j`, hence a rate dial, not a position dial. -/
theorem residueCarrier_periodic (m : ℕ) (N : ℤ) (g : ZMod m → α) :
    PeriodicClass m (fun j : ℤ => g (((j ^ 2 - N : ℤ) : ZMod m))) := by
  intro j
  have hcast : (((j + (m : ℤ)) ^ 2 - N : ℤ) : ZMod m) = ((j ^ 2 - N : ℤ) : ZMod m) := by
    push_cast [ZMod.natCast_self]
    ring
  simp only [hcast]

/-- The Legendre / quadratic-character carrier at a prime `p > 7` is a special
case: it is `p`-periodic. -/
theorem legendreCarrier_periodic (p : ℕ) [Fact (Nat.Prime p)] (N : ℤ) :
    PeriodicClass p (fun j : ℤ => quadraticChar (ZMod p) (((j ^ 2 - N : ℤ) : ZMod p))) :=
  residueCarrier_periodic p N (fun x => quadraticChar (ZMod p) x)

/-! ## Capstone: no residue mixture removes any part of the excess -/

/-- Cell-resolved reference sums built from a general classifier `f` and a window
of length `L`. -/
noncomputable def classRefSum (f : ℤ → α) (L : ℕ) (B : ℝ → ℝ) (c : α) (t : ℝ) : ℝ :=
  (count f ⌊t⌋ L c : ℝ) * B t

/-- A periodic classifier, sampled on windows whose length is a multiple of the
period, has flat composition in the sense of Part II. -/
theorem classRefSum_flatComposition {m : ℕ} {f : ℤ → α} (hper : PeriodicClass m f)
    {L q : ℕ} (hL : L = m * q) (B : ℝ → ℝ) :
    FlatComposition (classRefSum f L B) (fun c => (count f 0 L c : ℝ)) B := by
  intro c t
  simp only [classRefSum, count_const_of_period_dvd hper hL ⌊t⌋ c]

/-- **Capstone (follow-up to paper 242).**  For *any* residue-type carrier — any
`m`-periodic classification of `j`, at any modulus, sampled on windows of length
a multiple of `m` — the mixture baseline leaves the mid-window excess exactly as
it was: removal is `0 %`. -/
theorem residue_mixture_excess_survives [Fintype α] {m : ℕ} {f : ℤ → α}
    (hper : PeriodicClass m f) {L q : ℕ} (hL : L = m * q) (B T : ℝ → ℝ) (κ : α → ℝ)
    {t₀ t₁ : ℝ} (hK : (∑ c, κ c * (count f 0 L c : ℝ)) ≠ 0) (hT : T t₁ ≠ 0) (hB : B t₁ ≠ 0) :
    relExcess (resid T (mixPred κ (classRefSum f L B))) t₀ t₁ = relExcess (resid T B) t₀ t₁ :=
  relExcess_invariant (classRefSum_flatComposition hper hL B) κ hK hT hB

/-- **The follow-up, stated as a constraint on the carrier.**  If some class
mixture does move the measured excess, then the classifier is not periodic at
any modulus dividing the window length: the non-divisibility positional carrier
must be genuinely aperiodic in `j`, so no Legendre symbol, power residue,
divisibility pattern or bit pattern of `j² - N` can be it. -/
theorem positional_carrier_is_aperiodic [Fintype α] {f : ℤ → α} {L : ℕ}
    {B T : ℝ → ℝ} {κ : α → ℝ} {t₀ t₁ : ℝ}
    (hK : (∑ c, κ c * (count f 0 L c : ℝ)) ≠ 0) (hT : T t₁ ≠ 0) (hB : B t₁ ≠ 0)
    (hmoves : relExcess (resid T (mixPred κ (classRefSum f L B))) t₀ t₁ ≠
      relExcess (resid T B) t₀ t₁) :
    ¬ ∃ m q : ℕ, L = m * q ∧ PeriodicClass m f := by
  rintro ⟨m, q, hL, hper⟩
  exact hmoves (residue_mixture_excess_survives hper hL B T κ hK hT hB)

/-- The divisibility grid of Part I is one instance: `210 = 2·3·5·7`-periodic. -/
theorem cell_periodicClass (N : ℤ) : PeriodicClass 210 (cell N) := by
  intro j
  have : ((210 : ℕ) : ℤ) = (210 : ℤ) := by norm_num
  rw [this, cell_periodic]

end RateDial
